sample_unit: model-question responses (5 LLMs x 20 patient IBD questions)
models_evaluated: five publicly available LLMs (names not given in the abstract)

links.outcome: Readability of LLM answers to patient IBD questions versus patient targets
links.effect: Grade-level indices exceeded sixth grade; Flesch Reading Ease medians ranged from 15 to 36 versus a target of >=80 for easy readability.
links.quote: Readability consistently failed to meet patient targets, with grade-level indices exceeding sixth grade and Flesch Reading Ease medians ranging from 15 to 36 (compared to a target of ≥80 for "easy" readability).

links.outcome: Reading level of LLM patient-facing IBD answers relative to appropriate patient level
links.effect: Grade-level indices exceeded sixth grade; Flesch Reading Ease medians 15-36 (target >=80).
links.quote: Readability consistently failed to meet patient targets, with grade-level indices exceeding sixth grade and Flesch Reading Ease medians ranging from 15 to 36 (compared to a target of ≥80 for "easy" readability).

links.outcome: Comprehensibility of LLM responses for lay patients (readability indices)
links.effect: Readability indices consistently failed patient targets; grade levels exceeded sixth grade, and Flesch Reading Ease medians ranged 15-36.
links.quote: Readability consistently failed to meet patient targets, with grade-level indices exceeding sixth grade and Flesch Reading Ease medians ranging from 15 to 36 (compared to a target of ≥80 for "easy" readability).

links.outcome: Transparency proxies (JAMA benchmark) of LLM answers, including provenance and disclosure
links.effect: Transparency remained limited, with JAMA median 0-1/4 across models.
links.quote: Median DISCERN scores ranged from 43.5 to 57.5, and EQIP scores ranged from 67.5 to 77.5, while transparency remained limited (JAMA median 0-1/4).
